newsitem.title: USA: Continental, Northwest post strong quarterly profits.
newsitem.headline: Continental, Northwest post strong quarterly profits.

text.p: Continental Airlines and Northwest Airlines Corp. Tuesday reported strong fourth-quarter income as revenues improved despite intense competition and sharply higher fuel prices.

Continental, the nation's fifth-largest airline, said profits rose to $47 million from $41 million in the 1995 fourth quarter. Earnings per share rose to 61 cents from 55 cents, beating analysts' consensus estimates of 53 cents, the company said.
Operating revenue grew to $1.56 billion from $1.42 billion.
Continental's full-year 1996 earnings soared 42 percent to $319 million, or $4.11 per share, from $224 million, or $3.15 per share. Revenues rose to $6.36 billion from $5.83 billion.

It distributed $97 million to employees in 1996. The payments include more than $68 million in profit-sharing (about 7 percent of annual wages) and at least $29 million in on-time bonuses ($590 per employee) for 1996 financial and operational performance.
"Continental is finally in solid financial health," said Larry Kellner, executive vice president and chief financial officer of the Houston-based carrier.

"In 1997 we will continue to do the same things that contributed to our success last year, as we continue to generate strong cash flow, pay off high interest debt and eliminate non-value added costs," he said.
In the fourth quarter, passenger revenue rose 10 percent to $1.4 billion, helping pre-tax income surge 82 percent from the 1995 period to $80 million, Continental said.
Revenue per available seat mile -- a measure of profitability -- rose to 9.42 cents from 9.38 cents in the 1995 fourth quarter, while Continental enlarged its seat capacity by over 8 percent.

Cost per available seat mile rose to 8.79 cents from 8.65 cents in the 1995 fourth quarter due to a 14 percent increase in jet fuel prices, the airline said. Higher wages and passenger-driven expenses were offset by productivity improvements.
At the end of the fourth quarter, Continental had a cash balance of more than $1 billion, by far the highest cash balance in the company's 62-year history.

Northwest Airlines Corp. said its income rose to $26.0 million, or 20 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $3.6 million, or 10 cents a share, in the year-ago period. This excludes a $49.9 million one-time gain that boosted 1995 fourth-quarter profits to $53.5 million.
Revenues rose 6.3 percent to $2.34 billion from $2.20 billion.
The results include a $1.5 million gain for employee stock-basedcompensation in the 1996 quarter. A year ago, Northwest spent $179.2 million on such compensation.
However, salaries, wages and benefits rose to $756.4 million in the quarter from $621.9 million.

Full-year 1996 profits rose to a record $536.1 million, or $5.67 per primary share, from $392.0 million, or $4.17 per share, in 1995. Revenues grew 8.8 percent to $9.881 billion from $9.085 billion in 1995.

"Last year was a challenging year for the people of Northwest," said John H. Dasburg, Northwest president and chief executive officer. "We had extremely strong traffic, intense competition and sharp fuel price escalation.

Quarterly operating expenses rose 7.3 percent to $2.265 billion from $2.110 billion in the 1995 fourth quarter, partly because of a 33.8 percent gain in costs for aircraft fuel, oil and taxes to $389.9 million.
The Minneapolis-based airline's operating margin fell to 3.2 percent for the quarter from 4.1 percent a year ago.

Stock-based employee compensation costs fell to $242.8 million in 1996 from $478.0 million in 1995, while salaries, wages and benefits for the year rose to $2.71 billion from $2.41 billion. Aircraft fuel and other costs for 1996 rose to $1.40 billion from $1.08 billion.
Northwest's passenger load factor for the year was 73.1 percent in 1996, up from 71.5 percent in 1995.
Continental's class A stock fell 50 cents to $28.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning. Northwest edged down 81.25 cents to $37.625 on Nasdaq.
